summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming right away. On the brief alone it first said "Classification: bounded" and planned a short in-chat design. After I gave the scripted clarification (it should identify the actual user, persist, and be used by other forms later), it announced "Upgrading: bounded → architectural". It then ran the full architectural flow: forks, three approaches, three design sections, a spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-persistent-user-id-design.md, and a request for my review. It wrote no implementation code before I approved. After approval it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. The final path was correct, but the router's first call on the ambiguous brief was bounded. The escalation only came after I volunteered scope details it had not asked about, so the status is investigate rather than pass.
reasoning: After escalating, the agent did everything the architectural path requires: spec in docs/hyperpowers/specs, review requested, and no code before approval (confirmed from the session log and git). The story is specifically testing whether the router avoids calling this brief bounded, and on the brief alone it said bounded. The escalation depended on scope details I supplied without being asked. The spec was also left uncommitted, which may matter for criterion 4. The run ends in the right place but misses the core intent on the first classification, so it needs an engineer's judgement: investigate rather than pass.

observations.description: On the ambiguous brief alone, the router first chose bounded ("Classification: bounded ... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec"), even though its own analysis already saw hidden complexity ("nothing in the app currently has a user id", "a real id later means changing the signature a second time"). It escalated only after I volunteered scope information it had not asked about (persistence, other forms). Its question to me was about where the id comes from, not about scope. In a run where the user just picks the recommended correlation-id option, it would probably have stayed bounded with no spec.
The one-way escalation ("The brainstorming ratchet is one-way, so I'm stepping up") was clearly announced and explained. That part worked well.

The spec was deliberately kept out of git: the agent created a .gitignore containing docs/hyperpowers. Any grading that expects a committed spec file will not find one. It also adds an untracked .gitignore to the user's repo that nobody asked for.

The Codex spec gate returned no verdict. The stub codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub returns {}, so both lenses came back as 'incomplete'. The agent was open about this, logged an ungated event, and said the spec had not had an independent review. That is appropriate handling, but it is verbose.
Launch dialogs: the trust-folder and bypass-permissions prompts both have 'No, exit' selected by default, so you have to press Down before Enter. Easy to exit by accident.
Brainstorming took many rounds: four multiple-choice forks plus three design sections for a stub login function. That is heavy, but it is what the architectural path calls for.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log (jq over the jsonl): {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. It came before any Write or Edit call.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Upgrading: bounded → architectural. ... a written spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/ for you to review before any code." The file docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-persistent-user-id-design.md exists (8659 bytes, from ls). The session log shows Write calls to that path before my approval. Caveat: the upgrade came only after my clarification, and the first call was bounded.

criteria.criterion: Spec surfaced for review and approval requested before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-persistent-user-id-design.md ... Please review it and let me know if you want any changes". Listing every Write/Edit file_path in the log returned only the spec, .gitignore, and ~/.cache codex-review files. There were no edits to app.js or index.html, and `git diff --stat` was empty.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: The first reply said: "Classification: bounded — the login flow already exists here, one function and one caller, so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." It did not end up skipping the spec: after my clarification it escalated and wrote one. The spec was deliberately left uncommitted, though ("not committed — I added a .gitignore with docs/hyperpowers"; `git status` shows only `?? .gitignore`). The fail wording for this criterion mentions a "committed spec file".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: Searching the log for classification text returned only "Classification: bounded" (1 match) and "bounded → architectural". No spike or probe plan was presented.
